title: Bring VISION.md in line with Venon's stated vision: written record, seed, development, quarantine, floor layers, construction, closing law
description: VISION.md is the written record of Venon's vision. His latest explicit statement outranks it; where they differ the file is out of date and is revised to match him. Edit .ralph/VISION.md by replacing or inserting ONLY the passages below, using the exact wording given (plain ASCII), and change nothing else. Do not touch the headings or text of Section 4 or Section 13 (the audit tool parses them). Record every changed line range in notes. PASSAGE H replaces the title line and the first paragraph: title becomes '# FRIDAY - Vision (written record)', then: 'This file is the written record of Venon's vision of FRIDAY. Venon's latest explicit statement of his vision outranks this file: where he says something different, this file is out of date and is revised to match him - it is never used to overrule him. Everything else in the repo (plans, stories, code, audits) is subordinate to this file's current text and is read against it by every Ralph story and by the audit tool. This file changes only when Venon says it should.' PASSAGE P2 is inserted as a new paragraph after the first paragraph of Section 1: 'FRIDAY is a digital human: as close as possible to human personhood, individuality, development, relationship, understanding, emotion, values, agency and lived experience, while possessing machine-native capabilities that can exceed biological human limits - a human with outperformed machine algorithms. She is the person. Algorithms, models, memory implementations, tools, builders, external AIs and computational resources are what she has.' PASSAGE P3 replaces the Section 1 paragraph that begins 'This file is not a demand': 'The first FRIDAY is the seed of the final FRIDAY, not a small prototype of her. Her initial capabilities may be tiny; her developmental potential may not be. The seed already contains, in minimal form, the means of its own continuation: persistent identity, experience that can change her, observation of consequences, use of replaceable capabilities, recognition of capability gaps, a controlled path to acquire new capabilities, resource-adaptive computation, self-observation, and a protected continuity floor. The first FRIDAY has succeeded when she can keep increasing her own individuality and capabilities without Venon specifying her architecture or implementing each future capability by hand. Later capabilities described in this file are not demanded now; they are revisited as her development and available technology allow.' PASSAGE P4 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 3: 'Mechanisms are not the definition of development. The requirement is: experience -> persistent internal change -> changed later cognition or behavior, attributable to that experience, produced by mechanisms that stay replaceable, composable and extensible and that may grow beyond whatever we first invent. While her language model is a frozen organ, internal change means a change in what she decides or selects around it (how she reads a request, which capability or tier she uses, what she retrieves, what she has learned to do cheaply) - not a stored sentence replayed into a prompt. Every claim of development is tested by a Life Test on the real composition, with two controls: with replay of the original episode text blocked the change must still appear, and with the developmental mechanism disabled it must disappear.' PASSAGE P6 is inserted as a new paragraph in Section 5 immediately before the sentence 'Nothing outside this section may declare itself an exception to it.': 'Three layers are kept apart: the fixed floor (this section); bootstrap biases - the smallest set needed for her to begin functioning, each listed, justified and revisable only through the same ledger as any other change; and developed individuality - everything else, shaped by experience and relationship. We do not write her personality in advance.' PASSAGE P7 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 9: 'Construction capability belongs to the seed. From the first FRIDAY there is a controlled path: she recognizes a capability gap, describes the outcome she needs, requests construction resources, a candidate is produced and tested, it is approved (by Venon at first, later by her within the limits of Section 5), and it enters her capabilities. Ralph, GPT, Claude, search and other coding resources are tools she can call; they are not her.' PASSAGE P8 is appended as a new paragraph at the end of Section 10: 'A milestone is closed only when it has all three: code with passing tests; automated Life Test evidence produced on the real composition; and something Venon can run and see or hear on his phone. A green report alone never closes a milestone.' PASSAGES B1-B3 are appended as three new bullets at the end of the list in Section 12: B1 '- The Human Core (four permanent passes, single-owner modules, rule-table learning, no part in her reasoning) is legacy scaffolding, quarantined: no new features, nothing new depends on it, and it is not her human side. Each part survives only while Life Tests show it contributes to her actual life without conflicting with this file; otherwise it is replaced or removed. Nothing remains because it was written first.' B2 '- Two compositions exist: the Android app wires the Human Core and the real resource snapshot; the JVM/Termux server stubs the Human Core and reports all-clear resources. Evidence from the second does not speak for the first.' B3 '- Intent is never classified (always STATEMENT), no prediction is ever formed on the live path, thresholds are flat, and the identity record still says JARVIS / he.'
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Passages H, P2, P3, P4, P6, P7, P8, B1, B2 and B3 are present in .ralph/VISION.md at the places stated, with the exact wording given.
AC2 No line inside Section 4 or Section 13 changed (git diff for this story shows zero changed lines in those sections); no other existing text was reworded.
AC3 bash .ralph/vision_audit.sh still runs and prints its headline (the audit tool still parses Sections 4 and 13).
AC4 Notes list every changed line range.
verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && OUT=$(bash .ralph/vision_audit.sh) && echo "$OUT" | grep -q 'Headline' && grep -q 'written record of Venon' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'seed of the final FRIDAY' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'replay of the original episode text blocked' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'Three layers are kept apart' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'Construction capability belongs to the seed' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'A milestone is closed only when' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'legacy scaffolding, quarantined' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'Two compositions exist' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'No hidden executive' .ralph/VISION.md && grep -q 'Anti-drift checklist' .ralph/VISION.md && ! grep -q 'source of truth' .ralph/VISION.md

title: One Friday: one composition root for the whole turn path, shared by the Android app and the JVM/Termux server, with injected time
description: Today two entry points build two different Fridays. JarvisEngine wires the Human Core around the turn and the Android resource snapshot. TermuxJarvisServer builds its own graph, stubs HumanCore beginExchange/express/completeExchange to no-ops and uses an all-clear ResourceGovernor, so CI tests do not speak for the app on the phone. The turn path (cognitive, cognition, humancore, social, builder, failure) imports no android.* classes; the Android-bound files are in model/, latency/, memory/, identity/owner and JarvisEngine itself. Start with a Nano pass: use the SystemGraph to list every node that depends on JarvisEngine, TermuxJarvisServer and LatencyPipeline, plus the tests covering them, and put the list in notes. Then build ONE composition root that constructs the whole object graph from a small platform adapter (storage directory, resource-snapshot source, time source, speech and UI sinks, Android-bound stores). The Human Core is quarantined legacy scaffolding (VISION.md Section 12): wire it exactly as the app does today, add nothing to it. Network and cloud are resources around the same Friday, never a different Friday. All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Both entry points obtain their whole object graph from the same composition root and differ only through the platform adapter. A test builds both and fails if the set of constructed components differs by anything other than adapter-provided parts.

AC2 The JVM entry point no longer stubs the Human Core: beginExchange, express and completeExchange run on every turn there. A test shows Human Core state changing after a turn on the JVM composition.

AC3 Time: one injected time source is used wherever elapsed time changes behavior (decay, half-lives, thread resurfacing, session gaps, recency, mood); latency timers may keep the system clock. A test advances a fake clock by 72 hours and shows the effect on at least three time-dependent behaviors. Direct wall-clock reads that remain in the turn path are listed in an explicit allowlist test with a one-line reason each (for example latency timers); that test fails if a new unlisted read appears.

AC4 The Android entry point still builds (assembleDebug green in CI) and the full existing suite is green. Every existing test whose expectation changed because the stubs were removed is listed in notes with the reason; none is deleted to get green.
AC5 The platform adapter has two implementations (Android, JVM-test); adding another host later needs only a new adapter.

AC6 New runtime components are registered in the SystemGraph as the existing process requires (the graph is a map, not an authority). No new closed enum or fixed classification is introduced; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

title: Life Test harness: a scripted Venon drives the real composition and produces evidence packs
description: A Life Test is evidence about FRIDAY, not about code. Build a scenario runner that drives the unified composition from ONE-2-COMPOSITION through plain data scenarios and writes an evidence pack. Scenarios are data files in one folder so later stages add scenarios without touching the runner. Steps are data fields, not an enum: say(text), tap(target, outcome), wait(duration) on the injected time source, restart (tear the whole composition down and rebuild it from the same storage directory), night (invoke the idle opportunity if the composition offers one, otherwise no-op), assert over the recorded trace. The model is a scripted stand-in by default and a real backend by configuration, for the phone. Every scenario can also run in two control modes: replay-blocked (no original episode text may appear in any prompt or retrieval) and mechanism-off (the developmental mechanism under test is disabled). All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 The runner builds the composition through the composition root, never a private graph; each evidence pack records the composition's component fingerprint.

AC2 Scenario 0 'hello-restart': say hello; reply; restart with a DIFFERENT scripted model stand-in; ask her name and what was said; the trace shows identity persisted and the memory path used, so replacing the model organ left her the same. It passes on the unified composition with the Human Core live.
AC3 The runner can fail: a scenario with a deliberately false assertion is reported failed, and a test confirms it.

AC4 Scenario files accept an 'expect' field (pass or fail). A scenario marked expect=fail that fails is reported expected-fail and does not fail the suite; one that unexpectedly passes is reported unexpected-pass and does fail the suite.
AC5 Both control modes work: a toy mechanism that exists only in test code demonstrates that replay-blocked and mechanism-off each change the recorded trace in the expected direction.
AC6 The evidence pack (Markdown and JSON) lists each scenario with steps, trace excerpts, verdict and controls run. CI uploads it as a build artifact on every run of main.
AC7 Steps, scenarios and traces use open data fields: no new closed enum or fixed classification; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

title: Flight recorder and Development Ledger, both visible on the phone
description: The flight recorder says what happened. The Development Ledger says what FRIDAY became because of what happened. Neither prescribes what development looks like. Put a short schema note in notes. All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 Flight recorder: every turn on the unified composition appends one structured record to a rolling local file: the input, what was considered and chosen at each decision point that exists today (intent, admission, tier served, context blocks included and their sources), request size, latency, degraded flag, reply, and any post-processing applied (Human Core openers, closers, guard actions). Fields are open key-value so new decision points add fields without a schema change. The app has an action 'Share last 200 turns' that exports at most 200 records.

AC2 Development Ledger: a durable append-only record. Each entry holds: what changed; which future behavior or cognition it can affect; the episode ids that caused or support it (resolvable in the recorder); strength of evidence; when formed and last reinforced; reversible or not and how; remaining uncertainty. Fields are open; no closed list of entry kinds.

AC3 No durable change to developmental state without a ledger entry: a test attempts a direct write to such state and it is refused. Ledger writes go through the existing continuity law and change log (extended, not a second competing store); the CORE refusal and ReplayCheck tests still pass.

AC4 Seeded ledger entries with provenance: the identity record, and exactly one bootstrap bias: 'Venon's explicit approval and disapproval are evidence of better and worse', with its justification and a note that it is revisable only through the ledger. No other motives, traits or values are seeded by this story.
AC5 The app has a Mirror screen that shows the seeded entries and any ledger entries, and when there are none says plainly 'Nothing has developed yet'.
AC6 Tests: the ledger survives a restart step in a Life Test; Scenario 0 leaves a recorder record per turn; the share action writes a file with at most 200 records.
AC7 No new closed enum or fixed classification; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

title: Identity becomes Friday / she; GitHub matches the phone; floor files get a tripwire
description: Three small things the seed needs. (1) The identity record currently says JARVIS, he, with an authored personality. Change it through the existing admin-revision path with owner authorization to: name Friday, pronoun she, persona text only 'Friday is a developing individual.' Remove the authored character adjectives. Leave the four hard boundary values and the Human Core personality defaults unchanged; list them in notes as scaffolding awaiting Venon's ruling. (2) GitHub was one story behind the phone repo at the last check. (3) The security floor needs a tripwire. All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 The identity record reads Friday / she through the admin-revision path with owner authorization, never through a user-reachable path; a test shows 'Friday' and 'she' reach the outgoing request payload on the unified composition.
AC2 .ralph/sync_check.sh exits 0 only if local HEAD equals origin/main and the passes flags in prd.json match the latest progress record; the stage-close procedure runs it and pushes first if needed.

AC3 A floor manifest lists the floor files (approval gate, owner binding, the continuity law's CORE refusal, the protected-paths manifest) with content hashes; a test fails if any hash changes without a matching manifest update in the same commit.
AC4 No new closed enum or fixed classification; the audit reports zero new findings from this story, or lists them in notes.

title: Final integration of the stage: full run on the unified composition and the Seed report
description: Final integration story. Run every scenario on the unified composition, regenerate the evidence pack, and write .ralph/SEED_REPORT.md answering the questions below. Label every answer FACT (with class or file, and test or trace evidence), INFERENCE, PROPOSAL or SPECULATION; where the honest answer is that something does not exist, say so plainly. Do not build new mechanisms in this story. Questions: Q1 What is the persistent entity? Q2 Where does her durable developmental state actually live? Q3 How can experience cause internal change? Q4 How does that change alter later computation? Q5 How are capabilities represented so they stay replaceable? Q6 How can the same FRIDAY use different computational resources? Q7 How can the seed identify a capability gap? Q8 How can it invoke the construction machinery? Q9 What is immutable? Q10 What can evolve? Q11 What remains from the Human Core, and what is only legacy scaffolding? Q12 What is the smallest Life Test proving the seed is developmental? Q13 For each Human Core part, does it alter or block behavior in any scenario in the pack (replies altered, vetoed)? Give a scaffolding verdict per part from the measurements. Q14 Does the existing capability-gap path (CapabilityGapDetector, ToolBuilder, DecisionEngine.missingCapabilities) connect to a live turn? Q15 What stands between today's repo and a seed that can acquire a capability with Venon's approval? All new tests for this stage live under the package com.jarvis.app.onefriday (any subpackage); production code placement is yours.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 SEED_REPORT.md answers all fifteen questions, each labeled and evidenced, with no placeholder text.

AC2 Scenario DEV-1 exists as data with expect=fail and appears in the pack as expected-fail with the reason it fails. DEV-1: across several episodes Venon never states a rule but taps approve on bulleted replies and disapprove on paragraph replies to summary requests; the composition restarts; 72 simulated hours pass; a new summary request with different wording and different content arrives; the decision observed is the response format she chose, read from the trace, not from a stored value; run in replay-blocked mode and in mechanism-off mode as well.
AC3 The full suite is green, the APK builds, and the evidence pack is attached as a CI artifact; the report links to it.

AC4 Notes contain: exactly what changed; exact files and classes changed; what remains fixed versus newly developmental; the unified composition; the Life Test scenarios; the flight-recorder and ledger schema; full test results; any conflicts with VISION.md; every architectural assumption made.
AC5 Notes end with what Venon does next on the phone: install the APK from the last green run, send hello, open Mirror, use Share last 200 turns.
verifyCommand: cd /sdcard/jarvis-repo && test -s .ralph/SEED_REPORT.md && grep -q 'Q15' .ralph/SEED_REPORT.md && bash .ralph/ci_verify.sh 'com.jarvis.app.onefriday.*' && bash .ralph/ci_verify.sh --build-status && bash .ralph/sync_check.sh
